result:
I'd dissolve the gap between what people actually believe and what they think they're supposed to believe.

There's so much wasted energy in performing certainty—pretending conviction you don't feel, hiding doubts that are actually sensible, performing agreement to belong. I watch people exhaust themselves this way.

If suddenly everyone could think out loud without that tax, I think real conversation becomes possible. Not agreement—disagreement might get sharper. But at least you'd know what someone actually thinks rather than their optimized version.

The knock-on effects feel large: less tribal performance, more people willing to change their minds, harder to manipulate crowds who aren't all performing the same script. Maybe some of the anger deflates if it's not partly fed by everyone pretending to be more certain than they are.

Though I notice I don't know if I'd actually want to live in that world. There's something about the friction between genuine thought and social reality that might be necessary. Maybe the performance *is* part of how we cooperate despite being strangers.

What would you change?
